title: Open a phone's glued-on display like a book without tearing its cables, and lean it on its stand
instruction: This phone's display is glued to its frame along its right edge and the right halves of its top and bottom edges, and joined to the phone by short cables along its left edge. Using the tools on the cradle, free the display from all of its adhesive and open it like a book over its left edge until it leans on the foam block, never opening it further than that. Then put both tools down on the cradle, clear of the phone and with nothing left stuck to the display, and take both arms back to where they started.
context: Opening a phone whose display is glued to its frame is the first step of most smartphone repairs (screens, batteries, cameras). A technician lifts the glass with a suction cup just enough to slip a thin tool into the seam, cuts the adhesive along the free edges, and opens the display no further than its short flex cables allow; opening it too far tears them.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A repair cradle, fixed: a blue-grey anti-static mat on a slab 1.2 cm thick, from 12.5 to 37.5 cm forward and from 15 cm right to 17.5 cm left of the centre line. (2) A smartphone (about 180 g) in the cradle's recess, held by it, face up, its long side running forward, its middle 25 cm forward on the centre line; the cradle's top is flush with the seam under its display. Its display assembly (black glass over the OLED panel, 14.76 x 7.16 cm, 3 mm thick, 45 g) is glued to the aluminium frame by an adhesive strip along its whole right edge and along the right halves (3.6 cm) of its top and bottom edges, and joined along its left edge by two short flex cables, about which it can swing open like a book up to a stop at 115 degrees; under it are the battery and the logic board. (3) A foam block 10 cm long, 2.2 cm wide and 3.5 cm tall, fixed on the cradle left of the phone, from 4.5 to 6.7 cm left of the centre line, centred 25 cm forward: the display opened over its left edge leans on it at about 100 degrees. (4) An opening tool (25 g): a blue ABS handle 8.5 x 1.6 x 1.4 cm with a flat stainless blade 4.5 cm long, 1.4 cm wide and 1.5 mm thick, lying flat on the cradle 19.5 cm forward, its blade pointing left at the phone's right edge with its tip 2.5 cm from it. (5) A suction cup (30 g): a grey silicone cup 4 cm across under a grey ABS handle 1.6 cm thick and 3.5 cm tall, standing on the cradle 19 cm forward and 10.5 cm left of the centre line. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: The display's opening is its turn about its left (cable) edge. An adhesive segment (seven: the right edge in three, the right halves of the top and bottom edges in two each) comes free for good once the opening tool's blade is in the seam under it: under the display's underside by at most 2.5 mm, inside its outline at least 2 mm and at most 16 mm in from that edge, within that segment's stretch. 0.0 if the display is ever opened past 108 degrees or its cable edge pulled 5 mm off its line (the cables torn; latched). Otherwise 1.0: at the end every segment free, the display open between 80 and 108 degrees, both tools on the cradle clear of the phone (more than 1 cm outside its outline, lying or standing under 20 degrees from their resting attitude) with the suction cup not stuck to the display, and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start); 0.75: every segment free and the display open between 80 and 108 degrees at the end; 0.5: every segment free at the end; 0.25: the blade in the seam under the display at some point; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the display and both tools still.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the flex cables are a hinge; the adhesive is seven segments acting as springs against the display's turn (7 N m/rad together), each freed when the blade is in the seam under it. The cup's seal is a joint switched on when it is held flat on the glass and off past a 11 N pull or a 6 mm slide. Blade 1.5 mm thick, gap about 3 mm (real: 0.4 and 1 mm). Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
